problem: Addition: source says 'all the negroes born after a certain period shall be free'; candidate narrows to 'Black children born'.
replacement: It is clear that the southernmost States of the Union cannot abolish slavery without running very great dangers, ones the North had no reason to fear when it freed its Black population. We have already described how the Northern States manage the transition from slavery to freedom: they keep the present generation in chains and set their descendants free. In this way Black people are brought into society gradually. While the men who might abuse their freedom remain in servitude, those who are freed can learn the art of being free before they become their own masters. But this method would be hard to apply in the South. To declare that all Black people born after a certain date shall be free is to introduce the principle and the idea of liberty into the heart of slavery. The Black people whom the law keeps enslaved, while their children are released from that condition, are astonished at so unequal a fate, and their astonishment is only the prelude to impatience and resentment. From then on, slavery loses in their eyes the kind of moral power it drew from time and habit; it is reduced to a plain abuse of force. The Northern States had nothing to fear from this contrast, because Black people there were few and the white population was very large. But if this faint dawn of freedom were to show two million men their true position, the oppressors would have reason to tremble. Once they had freed the children of their slaves, the Europeans of the Southern States would very soon be obliged to extend the same benefit to the entire Black population.
